findings.description: Opening up ports to connect out to the public internet is generally to be avoided. You should restrict access to IP addresses or ranges that are explicitly required where possible.
findings.remediation: Set a more restrictive cidr range
findings.title: A security group rule should not allow unrestricted egress to any IP address.

findings.description:
Security groups provide stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS
resources. It is recommended that no security group allows unrestricted ingress access to
remote server administration ports, such as SSH to port 22 and RDP to port 3389.
findings.remediation: Set a more restrictive CIDR range
findings.title: Security groups should not allow unrestricted ingress to SSH or RDP from any IP address.

findings.description:
Security group rules should include a description for auditing purposes.

Simplifies auditing, debugging, and managing security groups.
findings.remediation: Add descriptions for all security groups rules
findings.title: Missing description for security group rule.

findings.description:
Security group rules should include a description for auditing purposes.

findings.remediation: Add descriptions for all security groups rules
findings.title: Missing description for security group rule.

findings.description: When using a 'FROM' statement you should use a specific tag to avoid uncontrolled behavior when the image is updated.
findings.remediation: Add a tag to the image in the 'FROM' statement
findings.title: ':latest' tag used

findings.description: Running containers with 'root' user can lead to a container escape situation. It is a best practice to run containers as non-root users, which can be done by adding a 'USER' statement to the Dockerfile.
findings.remediation: Add 'USER <non root user name>' line to the Dockerfile
findings.title: Image user should not be 'root'

findings.description: You should add HEALTHCHECK instruction in your docker container images to perform the health check on running containers.
findings.remediation: Add HEALTHCHECK instruction in Dockerfile
findings.title: No HEALTHCHECK defined

findings.description: 'apt-get' install should use '--no-install-recommends' to minimize image size.
findings.remediation: Add '--no-install-recommends' flag to 'apt-get'
findings.title: 'apt-get' missing '--no-install-recommends'

findings.description: A program inside the container can elevate its own privileges and run as root, which might give the program control over the container and node.
findings.remediation: Set 'set containers[].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation' to 'false'.
findings.title: Can elevate its own privileges

findings.description: The container should drop all default capabilities and add only those that are needed for its execution.
findings.remediation: Add 'ALL' to containers[].securityContext.capabilities.drop.
findings.title: Default capabilities: some containers do not drop all

findings.description: Security best practices require containers to run with minimal required capabilities.
findings.remediation: Specify at least one unneeded capability in 'containers[].securityContext.capabilities.drop'
findings.title: Default capabilities: some containers do not drop any

findings.description: Sharing the host’s network namespace permits processes in the pod to communicate with processes bound to the host’s loopback adapter.
findings.remediation: Do not set 'spec.template.spec.hostNetwork' to true.
findings.title: Access to host network

findings.description: Enforcing CPU limits prevents DoS via resource exhaustion.
findings.remediation: Set a limit value under 'containers[].resources.limits.cpu'.
findings.title: CPU not limited

findings.description: Force the running image to run as a non-root user to ensure least privileges.
findings.remediation: Set 'containers[].securityContext.runAsNonRoot' to true.
findings.title: Runs as root user

findings.description: It is best to avoid using the ':latest' image tag when deploying containers in production. Doing so makes it hard to track which version of the image is running, and hard to roll back the version.
findings.remediation: Use a specific container image tag that is not 'latest'.
findings.title: Image tag ":latest" used

findings.description: An immutable root file system prevents applications from writing to their local disk. This can limit intrusions, as attackers will not be able to tamper with the file system or write foreign executables to disk.
findings.remediation: Change 'containers[].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem' to 'true'.
findings.title: Root file system is not read-only

findings.description: When containers have resource requests specified, the scheduler can make better decisions about which nodes to place pods on, and how to deal with resource contention.
findings.remediation: Set 'containers[].resources.requests.cpu'.
findings.title: CPU requests not specified

findings.description: When containers have memory requests specified, the scheduler can make better decisions about which nodes to place pods on, and how to deal with resource contention.
findings.remediation: Set 'containers[].resources.requests.memory'.
findings.title: Memory requests not specified

findings.description: Privileged containers share namespaces with the host system and do not offer any security. They should be used exclusively for system containers that require high privileges.
findings.remediation: Change 'containers[].securityContext.privileged' to 'false'.
findings.title: Privileged

findings.description: Enforcing memory limits prevents DoS via resource exhaustion.
findings.remediation: Set a limit value under 'containers[].resources.limits.memory'.
findings.title: Memory not limited

findings.description: Force the container to run with user ID > 10000 to avoid conflicts with the host’s user table.
findings.remediation: Set 'containers[].securityContext.runAsUser' to an integer > 10000.
findings.title: Runs with UID <= 10000

findings.description: Force the container to run with group ID > 10000 to avoid conflicts with the host’s user table.
findings.remediation: Set 'containers[].securityContext.runAsGroup' to an integer > 10000.
findings.title: Runs with GID <= 10000

findings.description: According to pod security standard 'Seccomp', the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile must be required, or allow specific additional profiles.
findings.remediation: Set 'spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type', 'spec.containers[*].securityContext.seccompProfile' and 'spec.initContainers[*].securityContext.seccompProfile' to 'RuntimeDefault' or undefined.
findings.title: Runtime/Default Seccomp profile not set

findings.description: A program inside the container can bypass Seccomp protection policies.
findings.remediation: Specify seccomp either by annotation or by seccomp profile type having allowed values as per pod security standards
findings.title: Seccomp policies disabled

findings.description: Containers should be forbidden from running with a root UID.
findings.remediation: Set 'securityContext.runAsUser' to a non-zero integer or leave undefined.
findings.title: Containers must not set runAsUser to 0

findings.description: Containers must drop ALL capabilities, and are only permitted to add back the NET_BIND_SERVICE capability.
findings.remediation: Set 'spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities.drop' to 'ALL' and only add 'NET_BIND_SERVICE' to 'spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities.add'.
findings.title: Container capabilities must only include NET_BIND_SERVICE

findings.description: Checks whether a workload is running in the default namespace.
findings.remediation: Set 'metadata.namespace' to a non-default namespace.
findings.title: Workloads in the default namespace

findings.description: The ports which are lower than 1024 receive and transmit various sensitive and privileged data. Allowing containers to use them can bring serious implications.
findings.remediation: Do not map the container ports to privileged host ports when starting a container.
findings.title: Prevent binding to privileged ports

findings.description: Security context controls the allocation of security parameters for the pod/container/volume, ensuring the appropriate level of protection. Relying on default security context may expose vulnerabilities to potential attacks that rely on privileged access.
findings.remediation: To enhance security, it is strongly recommended not to rely on the default security context. Instead, it is advisable to explicitly define the required security parameters (such as runAsNonRoot, capabilities, readOnlyRootFilesystem, etc.) within the security context.
findings.title: Default security context configured

findings.description: By enabling encryption on EBS volumes you protect the volume, the disk I/O and any derived snapshots from compromise if intercepted.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption of EBS volumes
findings.title: EBS volumes must be encrypted

findings.description: Encryption using AWS keys provides protection for your EBS volume. To increase control of the encryption and manage factors like rotation use customer managed keys.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption using customer managed keys
findings.title: EBS volume encryption should use Customer Managed Keys

findings.description: S3 buckets should block public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By blocking, PUTs with fail if the object has any public ACL a.
findings.remediation: Enable blocking any PUT calls with a public ACL specified
findings.title: S3 Access block should block public ACL

findings.description: S3 bucket policy should have block public policy to prevent users from putting a policy that enable public access.
findings.remediation: Prevent policies that allow public access being PUT
findings.title: S3 Access block should block public policy

findings.description: Ensures S3 bucket logging is enabled for S3 buckets
findings.remediation: Add a logging block to the resource to enable access logging
findings.title: S3 Bucket Logging

findings.description:
Versioning in Amazon S3 is a means of keeping multiple variants of an object in the same bucket.

You can use the S3 Versioning feature to preserve, retrieve, and restore every version of every object stored in your buckets.

With versioning you can recover more easily from both unintended user actions and application failures.

When you enable versioning, also keep in mind the potential costs of storing noncurrent versions of objects. To help manage those costs, consider setting up an S3 Lifecycle configuration.
findings.remediation: Enable versioning to protect against accidental/malicious removal or modification
findings.title: S3 Data should be versioned

findings.description: S3 buckets should ignore public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By ignoring rather than blocking, PUT calls with public ACLs will still be applied but the ACL will be ignored.
findings.remediation: Enable ignoring the application of public ACLs in PUT calls
findings.title: S3 Access Block should Ignore Public ACL

findings.description: Buckets should not have ACLs that allow public access
findings.remediation: Don't use canned ACLs or switch to private acl
findings.title: S3 Buckets not publicly accessible through ACL.

findings.description: S3 buckets should restrict public policies for the bucket. By enabling, the restrict_public_buckets, only the bucket owner and AWS Services can access if it has a public policy.
findings.remediation: Limit the access to public buckets to only the owner or AWS Services (eg; CloudFront)
findings.title: S3 Access block should restrict public bucket to limit access

findings.description: Opening up ports to connect out to the public internet is generally to be avoided. You should restrict access to IP addresses or ranges that are explicitly required where possible.
findings.remediation: Set a more restrictive cidr range
findings.title: A security group rule should not allow unrestricted egress to any IP address.

findings.description:
Security groups provide stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS
resources. It is recommended that no security group allows unrestricted ingress access to
remote server administration ports, such as SSH to port 22 and RDP to port 3389.
findings.remediation: Set a more restrictive CIDR range
findings.title: Security groups should not allow unrestricted ingress to SSH or RDP from any IP address.

findings.description:
Encryption using AWS keys provides protection for your S3 buckets. To gain greater control over encryption, such as key rotation, access policies, and auditability, use customer managed keys (CMKs) with SSE-KMS.
Note that SSE-KMS is not supported for S3 server access logging destination buckets; in such cases, use SSE-S3 instead.
findings.remediation: Use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK)
findings.title: S3 encryption should use Customer Managed Keys
